claims.statement: Normal dcode startup captures a workspace and resolved ServerConfig, scaffolds and starts a loopback LangGraph server on an ephemeral-port default, waits for the agent graph, configures the RemoteAgent workspace policy, and stops the owned server in a finally block if handoff does not complete, including cancellation.

For context-bearing server execution, make_graph requires a nonempty thread ID and workspace context, validates the durable thread workspace binding, and selects a binding-specific runtime; without execution context it returns the configured server runtime.

Server runtime construction returns the compiled agent, its CompositeBackend, and an offload operation derived from that same backend; process construction is lock-protected and cached, while workspace runtimes are a lock-protected LRU of at most 32 entries that reject configuration-policy drift and prevent a process-wide sandbox from being shared by different workspaces.

RemoteAgent delegates SSE parsing, stream negotiation, namespace extraction, and interrupt detection to RemoteGraph, requires a thread ID, forwards workspace context, converts streamed message dictionaries and interrupt updates for the UI, and leaves state snapshots serialized.

RemoteAgent treats a missing remote thread or a no-checkpoint SDK state-shape failure as empty state, but re-raises other state-read failures; it idempotently registers a live HTTP thread so checkpointed state can be mutated after server restart.
On a remote state-update conflict, RemoteAgent cancels pending and running runs with bounded concurrent waits and retries the update once.

CodeModelRetryMiddleware wraps model-node calls rather than an entire agent turn and reads retry budget from the request model when present; it is installed inside compaction so failed provider attempts do not replay completed tools, summary generation, or archive append.

Model retries re-raise GraphBubbleUp, retry only classified transient failures while budget remains, honor usable Retry-After hints or jittered exponential backoff, and re-raise terminal errors rather than fabricating an AI response; interactive retries have a cumulative delay guard.

Retry middleware emits correlated model attempt and retry stream events, tracks whether a failed attempt may have streamed visible output, and reports event-emission failures without failing the run so consumers can mark superseded partial output as incomplete.

Recovery abandons stale pending graph work by cancelling active runs, adding error results only for unanswered calls in the trailing AI-message turn, writing __end__, and verifying that no queued node, task, or interrupt remains.

Server graph construction snapshots the selected workspace environment and credentials before building its runtime, offloads blocking setup from the event loop, builds conditional web/MCP tooling, and emits a DEEPAGENTS_STARTUP_ERROR marker before exit on construction failure; parent health checking extracts that marker on early child exit.

Focused tests verify cache and startup-marker contracts with injected builders, retry and stream behavior with fake models and transport errors, remote conversion/recovery behavior with doubles, and an in-memory queued-tools graph where abandonment clears pending work without executing the tool.

RemoteAgent keeps workspace policy configuration separate from per-thread durable binding: policy and fingerprint must be supplied together, first use posts the workspace payload to the thread workspace route, and the returned descriptor is cached by thread.

The server child environment strips PYTHONPATH from server startup while relaying it only through a dedicated inherited carrier for downstream execute commands; local launch uses noop auth and generated dcode operation routes opt into custom-route auth when a deployment configures it.

ServerProcess uses a dedicated POSIX process group for graceful group shutdown and SIGKILL escalation, while Windows uses Ctrl+Break then root-process termination and may leave a surviving descendant orphaned.

ServerConfig partitions a workspace payload into a client-claimable session policy and server-resolved project policy, so project settings that can enable checkout-scoped execution are never accepted merely from the client claim.

Experimental server extensions are loaded with workspace, mode, project-trust, and explicit-path inputs; extension load errors are warned, and active server extensions are shut down if later graph construction fails.
